scope_framing: Create a new canonical thread for the MSX/OutRun-inspired arena presentation request.

The request spans visual draw layers, gate spawning, decorative queue preview, HUD, and continuous transition verification; this is medium staged work requiring implementation spec before build approval.
validated_facts: main.js owns the central update/draw loop and imports buildBackground from js/ui/canvas.js.

main.js draw() clears the canvas, translates for screen shake, clips to arena.points, draws backgroundCanvas inside the clip, draws speed dot, onions, player, then arena border; without arena it draws backgroundCanvas full canvas before entities.
js/ui/canvas.js buildBackground currently creates radial blue/purple glows and star-like dots, which conflicts with the requested no-space/no-galaxy direction.
Arena.constrainCircle(...) keeps circles inside the convex arena; Arena exposes points and shape but no gate abstraction.
LevelManager.updateWave() preserves finite wave behavior through budgetRemains, belowCap, pressureOpenSince, spawnIntervalMs, and #spawnQueuedOnion().
LevelManager.#spawnQueuedOnion() currently picks a random world edge side, creates an Onion, constrains it into the arena, then increments spawnedOnions.
LevelManager.getWaveProgress() already returns queuedOnions as totalOnions - spawnedOnions.
Speed Dot / lightning lifecycle is in LevelManager updateSpeedDot(), consumeSpeedDot(), #spawnSpeedDot(), and #assignSpeedDotTarget(); rendering and pickup order are in main.js.
Player and Onion already expose speed boost state and draw proportional boost rings.
index.html and main.js already define right run HUD bindings for level, opinion, next wave progress, and onions cleared/total/left.

index.html still contains level-overlay and main.js still defines showLevelOverlay(); normal wave completion currently uses resetGame(nextLevel,false), playLevelupSfx(), showLevelToast(), and updateRunHud() without calling showLevelOverlay().
